title: Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits
abstract: arXiv:2610.30844v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) distillation has shown empirical promise for training language models, but its statistical guarantees and limits remain poorly understood. In particular, the effects of two design choices remain unclear: Does access to the teacher's full action distribution provide an advantage over observing only the probability it assigns to the sampled action? Must training trajectories come from the student (online distillation), or can teacher-generated trajectories (offline distillation) suffice? Our work takes a first step toward understanding the theory underlying these questions.   We study the sample complexity of online reverse-KL distillation under two feedback models: the teacher reveals either its full action distribution or only the probability of the student-generated action. translated_abstract: 反向Kullback-Leibler（KL）蒸馏在训练语言模型方面已展现出经验上的潜力，但其统计保证和极限仍未被充分理解。特别是，两种设计选择的影响尚不明确：获取教师的完整动作分布是否比仅观察其赋予采样动作的概率更具优势？训练轨迹是否必须来自学生自身（在线蒸馏），还是教师生成的轨迹（离线蒸馏）就已足够？我们的工作为理解这些问题背后的理论迈出了第一步。我们研究了在两种反馈模型下在线反向KL蒸馏的样本复杂度：教师要么揭示其完整的动作分布，要么仅揭示学生所生成动作的概率。我们为前者建立了极小极大界，并证明后者可能需要多得多的数据。相比之下，离线反（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究首次从理论上分析反向KL策略蒸馏的统计保证，证明当教师提供完整动作分布时在线蒸馏具有极小极大最优的样本复杂度，而仅观察采样动作概率或采用离线蒸馏则可能需要显著更多的数据。
en_tdlr: This work provides the first statistical analysis of reverse-KL policy distillation, establishing minimax sample complexity bounds for online distillation with full teacher action distributions, while showing that partial feedback or offline distillation may require substantially more data.
